backgroundEn: Ahmad Tibi was born in 1958 in Tayibe, the second of seven children. In 1983 he graduated with honors in medicine from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and in December 1986 was licensed as a physician; he began a gynecology residency at Hadassah Mount Scopus but was dismissed before completing it in 1987, and he is registered as a physician without a specialty. He began political activity while a student, and in 1984 met Yasser Arafat in Tunis, which Israeli law then prohibited. After the Oslo Accords, in 1993, he was appointed Arafat's advisor on Israeli affairs, and in 1998 he served as spokesperson for the Palestinian delegation at the Wye River summit. In 1995 he founded Ta'al with a group of Arab academics; it did not pass the electoral threshold in the 1996 elections, and in 1999 he joined a joint list with Balad and was first elected to the Knesset. He served continuously in the 15th to 25th Knessets and was Deputy Speaker of the Knesset in the 17th. In the 2026 elections he was placed second on the Joint List for Ta'al.

backgroundEn: Faten Kamal Ghattas was born on June 2, 1960 in Rama to communist activist parents, and is the third of their children. As a teenager he was a member of the Israeli Communist Youth League, chaired the student council at Hanna Mwais High School in Rama and in 1979 was elected to head the national committee of Arab high-school students. After high school he began studying philosophy at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and co-founded the Yuad orchestra in Rama, which he managed. In 1985 he went to the University of Sofia in Bulgaria, completed an MA in philosophy there, served as secretary of the Israeli Communist Party branch in the country, and in 2025 received a doctorate in political science from that university. After returning to Israel in 1990 he turned to management roles, and since 1997 he has run the Israel Cancer Association's work in Arab society, including raising awareness of the risks of hookah smoking. In the Communist Party he chaired the Central Control Committee in 2007-2012 and was a member of the Central Committee and political bureau in 2021-2025, and in the 18th and 19th Knesset elections he held the symbolic slots 65 and 80 on Hadash's list. For the 2026 elections he was chosen for the second slot on the Hadash list, fourth on the Joint List, after the candidacy of Ja'afar Farah was cancelled over harassment allegations.

backgroundEn: Bakhar Awawdeh was born in Kafr Kana and studied at a university. He directed the Center for Combating Racism and from 2009 to 2019 headed the Galilee Society, the Arab national association for research and health services. After the death of his father, Muhammad Fandi, the sons established a development and social advancement fund in his memory; it was formalized in 2023 and each year grants scholarships worth more than half a million shekels to more than 240 students from Kafr Kana and orphans. In 2024 he was among the founders of the Al-Oula association for advancing Arab students in higher education, and he serves on its board and on that of the Karama Center for Combating Racism. Awawdeh was among Balad's first activists since its founding in 1995 and is a member of the party's political bureau; on July 28, 2013 he was arrested at a protest against the Prawer Plan. In Balad's 2026 primaries he was chosen for the second slot on its Knesset list, after party leader Sami Abu Shehadeh, and he is fourth on the Joint List in the election.

backgroundEn: Maha Karkabi-Sabbah was born in 1971 and grew up in Shefa-'Amr. She completed a BA in education and sociology and an MA in sociology at the University of Haifa and a PhD in sociology at Tel Aviv University, and later did three postdoctoral fellowships, including at the School of Oriental and African Studies of the University of London. She has lectured at Bar-Ilan University, the University of Haifa's Center for the Study of the Family and Tel Aviv-Yafo Academic College, and is a senior lecturer in the Department of Sociology and Anthropology at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev. Her research deals with social change in Arab society in Israel, especially women's status in the family, the labor market and the political arena, and she is a member of Balad's central committee. In 2026 she was elected by a large majority to third place on Balad's list, eighth on the Joint List, and in response the B'tsalmo organization demanded that BGU's management suspend her from her job without pay until the end of the election period.

backgroundEn: Nihaya Washahi, born in 1975, lives in Ar'ara. She completed a BA in education at the University of Haifa, where she began her political path by joining Hadash's student cell in 1994, and worked in the education system with teenagers, including at-risk youth. She later completed an MA in educational administration at Jadara University in Jordan and in 2022 a PhD in educational administration and foundations of education at Al-Yarmouk University, and since then has been an instructor at Al-Qasemi College and a lecturer at Oranim College. In 1999 she was first elected to the secretariat of Hadash's Ar'ara branch, and later to the movement's council, national secretariat and bureau. She has been the party's public representative on the Ar'ara local council since 2013 and is a board member of Hadash's faction in the Teachers' Union. In 2026 Hadash's national council chose Washahi for the fifth slot on its list, and she is placed tenth on the Joint List.

backgroundEn: Bezalel Smotrich was born in 1980 in Hispin in the Golan Heights, the son of Rabbi Chaim Yerucham Smotrich, and grew up in Beit El. He attended the middle school of Yeshivat Shaalvim, Jerusalem for Youth high school and Yeshivat Kedumim for about six years, while studying for an LLB at Ono Academic College. At 28 he enlisted in the IDF and served for a year and four months as operations NCO in the Operations Directorate of the General Staff. In July 2005 he was arrested by the Shin Bet along with four other right-wing activists on suspicion of organizing road blockades during the protests against the disengagement plan, and after about six weeks was released without indictment. He was operations director of the Regavim movement, served as a Jewish Home MK in the 20th to 22nd Knessets, and since 2021 has led the Religious Zionist Party, for which he also served as an MK in the 24th and 25th Knessets. He was Minister of Transport from 2019 to 2020, and since 2022 has been Minister of Finance and a minister in the Defense Ministry responsible for settlements. In 2026 he heads the Religious Zionism list, run jointly with Zehut.

backgroundEn: Moshe Feiglin was born in 1962 in Haifa. He served as an officer in the IDF's ABC warfare unit and left as a captain, then founded a rappelling company. He co-founded the Zo Artzeinu movement in 1992, joined Likud in 2000 and ran several times for the leadership of the movement, including in 2012. He served as a Likud MK and Deputy Speaker of the Knesset in the 19th Knesset, and in 2015 founded the Zehut party, which he led in the 2019 and 2020 elections. For the 26th Knesset he formed a technical bloc with Bezalel Smotrich's Religious Zionist Party and was placed second on the joint list.

backgroundEn: Orit Strook was born in 1960 in Jerusalem, the eldest of three children of a traditional family of Hungarian origin; her father, Yehuda Cohen, was a researcher of nationalism in the European Union, and her grandmother was the poet Malka Natshar. She studied at the Hebrew University High School in Jerusalem and became religiously observant in the 11th grade. She did national service at Bikur Cholim Hospital and at a school in Migdal HaEmek, moved with her husband to Yamit ahead of the Sinai withdrawal, and after its evacuation went to live in the Jewish community of Hebron. From 2000 she headed the legal-political department of the Jewish community in Hebron, and in 2002 founded the Yesha human rights organization, which she headed as a volunteer. In the 17th Knesset elections she ran 13th for Tekuma and was not elected, and in the 18th Knesset she volunteered as manager of the Land of Israel lobby. She served as a Jewish Home MK in the 19th Knesset and as a Religious Zionism MK in the 24th and 25th, and since 2022 has been Minister of Settlements and National Missions. In 2026 she is placed third on the Religious Zionism list.

backgroundEn: Itamar Eitam was born in 1980 in Moshav Nob in the Golan Heights and grew up there; he is the second son of retired brigadier general Effi Eitam, a senior officer and former minister, and the educator Ilit. In 2026 he joined Religious Zionism and was placed sixth on the list run jointly with Zehut.
